utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Who was or is he, and when did you receive this list?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Ramadan Kelmendi was deputy chairman of the Democratic League of Kosova, the Mitrovica branch. And I received this document from him towards the end of June, after the war, and he said that he found it in the Mitrovica municipal building. And this includes the names of 66 people who, according to the Serbs, were to be shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we now produce this. And it's produced in the usual form, but I also have what is the witness's original document for inspection. I don't know if the Court wishes to see that or not, but I have it for inspection and it's available, if they want it. Can we distribute those first, please. Can you lay the original Cyrillic on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we lay the original Cyrillic on the ELMO, please, so that we can all see it in its original form. Focus on the heading, if the booth would be good enough. Now if we could put the English version on the ELMO, please, and let the witness have the Cyrillic version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Does this document have, at the top, reference to SP, expansion - can enlarge on - and then go on to say, "For the special unit." On the left-hand side, is there a reference to 12/2/99, Kosovska Mitrovica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Is the heading of the list "List of Siptars in Kosovska Mitrovica who need to be summarily liquidated"?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Is there then a list of 66 names, including, at 21, your own?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, we see the list is dated February 1999, but in fact is there included on this list the name of any person or persons who was already dead by that date, who died earlier?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which number or numbers?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Number 44, Enver Haljid from Lubovic village, Skenderaj municipality, who from 22nd to 29th was killed in Vushtrri commune, municipality. He was a teacher of Albanian language and literature in Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He died -- sorry, what date do you say he died?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: From the 17th to 29th when attack was organised in Cicavica mountain in September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We see that on the document we're looking at, there's a pen or pencil circle around 44. Do you know who put that circle round it?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: I did it. Also the number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And the significance of your circling numbers 1 and 2? Any significance in that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Because they were already killed on 24th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So 44 killed before the date -- the apparent date of the document, and the numbers 1 and 2 killed afterwards. If we look at the foot of the document in the original version and over to the second page of the draft translation, the translation, I beg your pardon, we see that the document ends: "Implementation," then Dejan Zone 1, Ratko Zone 2, Kasalovic Zone 4, and Ajeti Zone 5, special unit Commander Colonel Markovic," with, in the original, a signature following it, and then a reference to, "Other and additional details available from Commander M. M.," and indeed we can see on the original an official stamp at the bottom of the document. Are you able to recognise that official stamp or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Of what is it the stamp?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: This is the stamp of a Serbian organisation. I can't tell which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think I am now in a position to make good the deficit presentation that occurred when we were looking for the list left behind in relation to the burnt villages. Sixty-eight names referred to at the foot of, or in paragraph 10, but just to check on that, I'll ask the witness. Please just one of these to the witness first so I can make sure we're on the same lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just tell us, before we embark on any distribution of this document, what this document is, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: This is a document with the names and last names, birth dates, and the place of birth, the place where he worked for every one of the persons listed here. It was found in the police checkpoint of Frasher i Madh, Mitrovica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps I can now distribute that. If we can -- sorry. You can lay the Cyrillic original on the overhead projector with its title, briefly, so that those looking at the television screen may see the original, the format of the document. Then if we can hand that document to the witness and place the English translation onto the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This document is headed, "RPO, Reserve Police Station," with a reference number "Ke-NV-06", then it has, one to two, names starting Mirko Mihajlovic with the date of birth and the unit in which he was, or the title of the unit in which he was employed. It runs down through several other lists of the 2nd Platoon on the second page and the 2nd Platoon again on the third page. And apart from names and dates of birth, we also see such employment locations as the tobacco depot, the post office, hospital, public accounting service, and matters of that sort. This document, you say, was left behind in the place where the destruction of property had occurred that you told us about.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, do you have the original copy of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we have the original of this document immediately to hand, but if it's in the building, we'll get it for you by tomorrow certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you help us now, please, with issues of demography generally. How many villages comprise the Mitrovica municipality?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Mitrovica municipality is comprised of 52 villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Based on a census, what was your understanding of the total population of the municipality at the time with which we are immediately concerned, and before expulsions, of course?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: I'm not clear about the question. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was the total population of the municipality before people had been expelled?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: About 100 to 20.000 [as interpreted] inhabitants. I couldn't give you a precise figure. This is something like that. Eighty-five per cent of them were Albanians, while 15 per cent, the remainder, others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And of that you estimate 15 per cent remaining -- remainder. What part were the Serbs as opposed to other groupings?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Serbs were around 5.000. This is a proximate figure. I can't give you accurate figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Of those expelled from the Mitrovica area, in which direction did -- in which directions did they go?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: The forcibly displaced Albanians from the Mitrovica municipality were told by the Serbian police, paramilitary, and civilians who escorted them on the way to Albania to Montenegro and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How did people travel; on foot or in vehicles?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: The bulk of them travelled on foot, but there were also some who used their cars or other vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's the route to Albania. Were there routes to any other destinations?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: I said earlier that the direction to Albania -- they were given orders to go to Albania, Macedonia, and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How did they get to Macedonia or to Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: In Macedonia and Montenegro, they went by buses and various other means of transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And you've already told us about the charging for the bus. From your position, were you able to assess the total number of Albanians killed in the Mitrovica municipality between the 13th of March of 1999 and the 17th of June of 1999?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: As of 13 March 1999, up to 17th of June, 1999, in the Mitrovica municipality were killed 650 Albanians of both genders and of all ages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've already told us of the total estimated number of 80.000 who were expelled. Numbers of injured and missing, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Four hundred twenty-nine were injured by firearms. Two hundred seventy-nine are considered disappeared. Five thousand eight hundred forty-two were arrested and detained in the prison of Smrkonica in Vushtrri municipality, in the technical school of Mitrovica. Then they were forced to leave from there and go to Albania. When they were released from the above-mentioned prisons all documentation they had was burned, like IDs, passports driving licences, and other IDs they had on them. Three hundred of the arrested were imprisoned in Serbia from one year to 20 years' of imprisonment. Then when the amnesty was declared, the overwhelming majority of them was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And finally on statistics, can you help us with the number of premises, houses or shops or other premises of Kosovo Albanians that were burned or destroyed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I'd like to find out from the witness where does he get all this information, the data. Perhaps you're coming to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We've covered it in part, and I'll come to it in just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you help me first before we turn to His Honour Judge Robinson's questions with the statistics for houses and shops and so on destroyed?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: The numbers of houses, shops, and other facilities was 9.540 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now let's turn to the method of your collecting this information. You've told us that you stayed in the area, it being your duty to do so, and you've explained how you were hiding from Serbs on the street. What were your sources of information that enable you to provide the figures of dead, injured, wounded, and destroyed property?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: The Council for the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms in Mitrovica had its collaborators in every neighbourhood, in every village, and other activists who informed it of any cases of use of violence this office in Mitrovica. Also, during the wartime, the overwhelming majority of cases were identified by me in person, but other cases have been referred to me and informed to me by -- either orally or in writing by other activists and Albanians who were not activists but who witnessed with their own eyes what I said earlier. Regarding the prisoners, after the war, all of them came to the office of the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms in Mitrovica and issued statements on the time of their arrest until they returned to their own lands on what had happened to each and every one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And have you collated the various sources of information in order to be able to provide the statistics that you have?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI
utterances.text: Yes. I collated them even before the war, but during the war not with the purpose of coming here to this distinguished Chamber because we didn't know that, but because we wanted to have general statistics about what happened to the Albanians of our municipality. About most of the cases that occurred in the Mitrovica municipality, I have the original information which were referred to me either on that day or on the next day which I got from various information media outlets.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm coming to the other two short topics that are dealt with on the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That would be a convenient moment. Mr. Barani, we're going to adjourn now for the evening. Would you be back, please, to conclude your evidence tomorrow morning at half past nine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of February, 2002, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.08 p.m.,
